  1. com.sbancuz.offscreen.api

Your first window

To create a window, make a screen, pass it to OffscreenAPI.open, and keep the returned handle so your addon can close it when finished.

Requirements

Install the OffscreenCleanroom JAR in your instance’s mods/ folder. This guide uses Minecraft 1.12.2, Java 25 and Cleanroom 0.7.13-alpha or newer with the SDL/LWJGLY backend. You can follow it without ModularUI, HEI or CraftTweaker.

You must open and close windows on Minecraft’s main client thread. A client button or key handler is a suitable place to open one. If you are loading data on a worker thread, return to Minecraft’s client task queue before creating the window. Keep the screen class in your addon’s client code so a dedicated server does not load it.

Keep text crisp while resizing

Call window.guiScale(1) on the client thread to keep text and controls at one drawable pixel per GUI unit, regardless of window size. Use 2 for double-sized pixels, or 0 to follow Minecraft's GUI scale again. This changes the coordinate space for layout and input together; it does not resize the desktop window. Keep the returned window handle and close it through its usual lifecycle.

Java, Kotlin, GroovyScript and Scala 3 use window.guiScale(1); CraftTweaker uses window.guiScale(1); on its window facade. For button labels, button.pixelTextScale(2) selects a whole-number enlargement independently of button dimensions. Java's native button builder accepts pixelTextScale(2f). Prefer whole-number scales for Minecraft's bitmap font; fractional textScale remains available for fonts designed for it.

Create a screen

First, create a class that extends GuiScreen. Offscreen will call its drawing and input methods on the client thread. In this example, drawScreen fills the window with a dark background and draws a message in the center.

You can copy the class below, or download the complete HelloScreen.java example, which also includes an open() helper. Adjust the package declaration for your addon.

import net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiScreen;

public final class HelloScreen extends GuiScreen {
    @Override
    public void drawScreen(int mouseX, int mouseY, float partialTicks) {
        drawRect(0, 0, width, height, 0xFF17232D);
        drawCenteredString(fontRenderer, "Hello from a separate window!",
                width / 2, height / 2, 0xFFFFFF);
        super.drawScreen(mouseX, mouseY, partialTicks);
    }
}

width and height are Minecraft GUI units. They are not necessarily desktop pixels: Minecraft's GUI scale and the monitor's display density affect the conversion. Offscreen handles that conversion.

Open the window

To open the screen, call OffscreenAPI.open(HelloScreen::new) from your client action. The argument is a function that creates a fresh screen. open calls that function immediately and returns a Window handle.

Save that handle in your client controller. You will use the same handle to set the title, change the size and close the window. If you downloaded the complete example, its HelloScreen.open() helper performs the opening step for you.

import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.OffscreenAPI;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window;

// Keep this reference in your client controller if you want to close it later.
Window window = OffscreenAPI.open(HelloScreen::new);
if (OffscreenAPI.isOpen(window)) {
    OffscreenAPI.setTitle(window, "Hello window");
    OffscreenAPI.resize(window, 960, 640);
}
Arguments used to open and configure this window
CallArgumentWhat to pass
open(screenFactory)screenFactoryA function that creates a new screen, such as HelloScreen::new or () -> new HelloScreen(). Create a fresh instance for each open.
setTitle(window, title)window, titleThe returned handle and the text to display in its title bar. The example uses "Hello window".
resize(window, width, height)window, width, heightThe handle and positive dimensions in SDL window coordinates. The example requests 960 by 640; screen layout still uses Minecraft GUI units.

The result is a separate desktop window with your message in the center. Each call to open creates another window. If you want one tools window at a time, retain its handle and reuse it while OffscreenAPI.isOpen(window) returns true; see the complete reuse example.

Check OffscreenAPI.isOpen(window) before using the result. It accepts null and reports whether the native window is open. To check whether its screen is ready to use, call OffscreenAPI.isReady(window). This distinction matters when a synchronized screen is still waiting for the server.

For a GuiScreen, the library supplies the code that connects drawing, input and cleanup to the desktop window. This connection is called an adapter. If your screen uses a different framework, you can register an adapter or pass one explicitly:

Choose an opening method
MethodWhen to use it
open(screenFactory)Use the registered adapter for the screen type. Vanilla GuiScreen is supported automatically.
open(screenFactory, adapterFactory)Supply the function that connects one custom screen to window drawing and input. See HostUI for the required callbacks.
openCustom(screenFactory, chrome)Choose a custom title bar when creating the window. The appearance section below explains chrome and its options.

If the screen factory returns null, or no adapter can handle the screen, opening returns null. Exceptions from your factory, adapter setup or native creation propagate to the caller.

Navigation and closing

When you want to show another page in the same desktop window, call OffscreenAPI.push(window, screenFactory). Pass the saved window handle and a function that creates the child screen. Check that the window is still open first, because the user may have closed it since your previous action.

if (OffscreenAPI.isOpen(window)) {
    OffscreenAPI.push(window, HelloScreen::new);
}

The example uses another HelloScreen, so both pages look alike. Substitute your own screen class for a different page. To return to the previous page, call pop with the same window handle:

boolean wentBack = OffscreenAPI.pop(window);

Popping disposes the child adapter and reveals the retained parent. Do not reuse the popped child's adapter or dispose the parent yourself. The first screen is the root. Calling pop on it returns false and leaves it in place.

To finish using the window, you must release the handle your addon owns. Put the following call in your client controller’s teardown or disconnect handler, or in the action that closes this tool. Run it when the tool is finished; placing it immediately after open would close the new window at once.

OffscreenAPI.close(window);

close(window) releases the screens still in that window’s stack and destroys its native resources. It also ends an attached synchronized session. You can safely pass null or an already closed handle. Close only the handles your addon owns.

Choose an icon and window appearance

Client GUI/input action and teardown. Normal opens use the operating system’s title bar, including the usual Windows controls. Custom chrome is optional. It reserves its own strip above the content, so title-bar clicks do not reach widgets and screen coordinates start below it.

Place a square PNG such as 32 × 32 or 64 × 64 at assets/my_addon/textures/gui/window_icon.png, or supply it from a client resource pack. Resource names use my_addon:textures/gui/window_icon.png, not local file paths. Transparency is preserved. Each image axis must be between 1 and 1024 pixels. The icon belongs to this window and survives navigation and synchronized retries; OS taskbar grouping still follows platform policy.

Window appearance controls
ControlBehavior
buttons(minimize, middle, close)Any of the eight combinations: one, two, all three or none.
titleBar(false)Hide the entire custom bar and its controls, leaving a borderless window.
colors(argb, rgb)Set the bar background tint/alpha and the caption/control color.
resizable(false)Prevent native edge dragging. Explicit programmatic resize is still available. An ordinary maximize control is disabled when fixed-size.
fullscreenButton(true)The middle control enters/leaves true fullscreen, rather than ordinary maximize/restore. It can be used with a fixed-size window.
chrome.opacity(0.5)Fade only the custom bar, including its caption, icon and controls. Zero makes the strip fully transparent.
setOpacity(window, 0.5)Fade the whole native window. Zero is fully invisible but still open; restore it with opacity 1 or close its retained handle.

Both opacity controls are independent and accept finite values from zero to one. Custom-bar transparency needs the creation-time openCustom path: an ordinary opaque native window cannot acquire per-pixel alpha later without recreation. The examples request custom chrome up front and then set whole-window opacity separately. Opacity does not remove the configured hit-test regions or request click-through; pointer delivery through fully transparent pixels depends on the native window system.

For a synchronized panel, use factory.openOffscreen(chrome); CraftTweaker uses Windows.openSynchronizedCustom(factoryName, chrome). The same server permissions and container limits apply. To restore native chrome later, use OffscreenAPI.setChrome(window, null) or window.nativeTitleBar() in CraftTweaker. Hiding Close does not disable Alt+F4, OS commands, or the public close API.

import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.OffscreenAPI;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.WindowChrome;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window;
import net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiScreen;
import net.minecraft.util.ResourceLocation;
import java.io.IOException;

final class AppearanceExample {
    // Client GUI/input action: ordinary OffscreenAPI.open keeps Windows/OS chrome.
    static Window openStyledWindow() throws IOException {
        var chrome = WindowChrome.defaults()
            .colors(0xFF253441, 0xFFFFFF)
            .buttons(true, false, true) // Minimize, middle, Close: any combination.
            .resizable(false)
            .opacity(0.65f); // Custom bar only; its text/buttons fade too.
        Window window = OffscreenAPI.openCustom(() -> new GuiScreen() {
        }, chrome);
        if (!OffscreenAPI.isOpen(window)) throw new IllegalStateException("Window unavailable");
        try {
            if (!OffscreenAPI.setIcon(window,
                new ResourceLocation("my_addon",
                "textures/gui/window_icon.png")))
                System.out.println("The platform did not accept the icon");
            if (!OffscreenAPI.setOpacity(window,
                0.9f)) System.out.println("Window opacity unavailable");
            return window; // Retain this exact owner in your client controller.
        } catch (IOException | RuntimeException | Error failure) {
            OffscreenAPI.close(window);
            throw failure;
        }
    }
    // Client teardown: OffscreenAPI.close(window).
}
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.OffscreenAPI
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.WindowChrome
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window
import net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiScreen
import net.minecraft.util.ResourceLocation

// Client GUI/input action. Retain the result in your client controller.
fun openStyledWindow(): Window {
    val chrome = WindowChrome.defaults().colors(0xFF253441.toInt(), 0xFFFFFF)
        .buttons(true, false, true).resizable(false).opacity(0.65f)
    val window = requireNotNull(OffscreenAPI.openCustom({
        object : GuiScreen() {
        }
    },
        chrome))
    return try {
        if (!OffscreenAPI.setIcon(window,
            ResourceLocation("my_addon",
            "textures/gui/window_icon.png")))
            println("The platform did not accept the icon")
        if (!OffscreenAPI.setOpacity(window,
            0.9f)) println("Window opacity unavailable")
        window
    } catch (failure: Throwable) {
        OffscreenAPI.close(window)
        throw failure
    }
}
// Client teardown: OffscreenAPI.close(window). Ordinary open keeps native OS chrome.
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.OffscreenAPI
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.WindowChrome
import net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiScreen
import net.minecraft.util.ResourceLocation
import java.util.function.Supplier

// Client GUI/input action; retain this controller-owned handle through reload/teardown.
def openStyledWindow() {
    def chrome = WindowChrome.defaults().colors(0xFF253441 as int, 0xFFFFFF)
        .buttons(true, false, true).resizable(false).opacity(0.65f)
    def window = OffscreenAPI.openCustom({ new GuiScreen() {} } as Supplier, chrome)
    if (!OffscreenAPI.isOpen(window)) throw new IllegalStateException('Window unavailable')
    try {
        if (!OffscreenAPI.setIcon(window,
            new ResourceLocation('my_addon',
            'textures/gui/window_icon.png')))
            println('The platform did not accept the icon')
        if (!OffscreenAPI.setOpacity(window,
            0.9f)) println('Window opacity unavailable')
        return window
    } catch (Throwable failure) {
        OffscreenAPI.close(window)
        throw failure
    }
}
// Client teardown/reload: OffscreenAPI.close(window). Ordinary open keeps native OS chrome.
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.{OffscreenAPI, WindowChrome}
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window
import net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiScreen
import net.minecraft.util.ResourceLocation

// Client GUI/input action. Retain the exact result in your client controller.
def openStyledWindow(): Window =
    val chrome = WindowChrome.defaults().colors(0xFF253441, 0xFFFFFF)
        .buttons(true, false, true).resizable(false).opacity(0.65f)
    val window = OffscreenAPI.openCustom(() => new GuiScreen() {}, chrome)
    if !OffscreenAPI.isOpen(window) then throw new IllegalStateException("Window unavailable")
    try
        if !OffscreenAPI.setIcon(window,
            new ResourceLocation("my_addon",
            "textures/gui/window_icon.png")) then
            println("The platform did not accept the icon")
        if !OffscreenAPI.setOpacity(window,
            0.9f) then println("Window opacity unavailable")
        window
    catch
        case failure: Throwable =>
            OffscreenAPI.close(window)
            throw failure
// Client teardown: OffscreenAPI.close(window). Ordinary open keeps native OS chrome.
#side client
import mods.offscreencleanroom.Windows;
import mods.offscreencleanroom.Window;

// Call from an actual client GUI/input callback, never while loading this script.
function openStyledWindow() as Window {
    val chrome = Windows.chrome().colors(-14339007, 16777215)
        .buttons(true, false, true).resizable(false).opacity(0.65);
    val screen = Windows.screen("My window", 640, 400);
    screen.text("Content stays separate from the title bar", 12, 12, -1);
    val window = Windows.openCustom(screen, chrome);
    if (!window.icon("my_addon:textures/gui/window_icon.png"))
        print("Icon unavailable; keeping the current icon");
    if (!window.opacity(0.9)) print("Window opacity unavailable");
    return window; // Retain this handle; client teardown calls window.close().
}
// Unlike Java's checked IOException, an unreadable script icon returns false and is logged.
// Ordinary Windows.open(screen) keeps native Windows/OS chrome.

Java/Kotlin/Groovy/Scala resource loading can throw an I/O error; the examples close the newly created owner before propagating it. CraftTweaker’s icon method returns false and logs unreadable resources so scripts can retain their previous icon. A native setter returning false means the platform did not accept that feature; it is not a successful configuration. Native creation failures propagate before a handle is returned. Keep all these calls on the client thread.

Formatted captions and motion

A custom title bar can use the same formatted font as your addon, including a renderer supplied by Chromatic Codes. Offscreen passes full strings to a generic measuring/drawing bridge and does not require that mod. The hook covers the title and every control label. Default control ink automatically contrasts with the bar tint. See the five-language caption recipe and window and per-element animations. To add a picture, video or sound, follow the media guide.

Working with server state

The example screen only displays client-side information. It does not create a server-owned inventory or send button actions to a server. For that, use OffscreenSimpleFactory and ModularUI's synchronization. Register the factory on both sides. Minecraft still permits only one active slot container per player; additional desktop windows do not change that rule.

Directly hosting GuiInventory is intentionally rejected. HEI adapts supported container screens when installed; it does not make arbitrary unsynchronized containers safe.

Create a local screen

This defines screen content without opening a desktop window. The native examples extend Minecraft’s GuiScreen; the ZenScript version describes the same static content.

import net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiScreen;
public final class HelloScreen extends GuiScreen {
    @Override public void drawScreen(int x, int y, float partialTicks) {
        drawRect(0, 0, width, height, 0xFF17232D);
        drawCenteredString(fontRenderer, "Hello", width / 2, 24, 0xFFFFFF);
        super.drawScreen(x, y, partialTicks);
    }
}

import net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiScreen
class HelloScreen : GuiScreen() {
    override fun drawScreen(x: Int, y: Int, partialTicks: Float) {
        drawRect(0, 0, width, height, 0xFF17232D.toInt())
        drawCenteredString(fontRenderer, "Hello", width / 2, 24, 0xFFFFFF)
        super.drawScreen(x, y, partialTicks)
    }
}

import net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiScreen
class HelloScreen extends GuiScreen {
    @Override void drawScreen(int x, int y, float partialTicks) {
        drawRect(0, 0, width, height, 0xFF17232D as int)
        drawCenteredString(fontRenderer, 'Hello', (width / 2) as int, 24, 0xFFFFFF)
        super.drawScreen(x, y, partialTicks)
    }
}

import net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiScreen
class HelloScreen extends GuiScreen:
  override def drawScreen(x: Int, y: Int, partialTicks: Float): Unit =
    net.minecraft.client.gui.Gui.drawRect(0, 0, width, height, 0xFF17232D)
    drawCenteredString(fontRenderer, "Hello", width / 2, 24, 0xFFFFFF)
    super.drawScreen(x, y, partialTicks)

import mods.offscreencleanroom.Windows;
val hello = Windows.screen("Hello", 640, 480).background(-15260883);
hello.text("Hello", 24, 24, -1);

Coordinates inside a hosted screen are Minecraft GUI units. Window sizes are logical desktop units and may differ on scaled displays. Each open needs a fresh backing screen; a screen declaration can be reused.

Open a window, change its title, and close it

The opening code shows the screen in a desktop window, then sets its title and dimensions. Run it from a client button or key action and save the returned window. The final close call is a separate, later action: call it when the user finishes or when your controller is shutting down.

import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.OffscreenAPI;
var window = OffscreenAPI.open(HelloScreen::new);
if (OffscreenAPI.isOpen(window)) {
    window.setTitle("Tools");
    window.resize(960, 640);
    window.setClearColor(0xFF17232D);
}
// Later, from the client thread:
OffscreenAPI.close(window);

import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.*
val window = openWindow("Tools", 960, 640) { HelloScreen() }
window.setClearColor(0xFF17232D.toInt())
// Later, from the client thread:
OffscreenAPI.close(window)

def windows = mods.offscreencleanroom.windows
def window = windows.open({ new HelloScreen() }, 'Tools', 960, 640)
windows.configure(window) { current -> current.setClearColor(0xFF17232D as int) }
// Later; reload also closes only this registry's windows:
windows.close(window)

import com.sbancuz.offscreen.scaladsl.Offscreen.*
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.OffscreenAPI
val window = open("Tools", 960, 640)(new HelloScreen)
window.setClearColor(0xFF17232D)
// Later, from the client thread:
OffscreenAPI.close(window)

// Inside a client GUI/input callback, after declaring hello:
val window = hello.open();
window.title("Tools");
window.resize(960, 640);
window.clearColor(-15260883);
// Later, while retaining this exact handle:
window.close();

Closing releases this window’s adapters and synchronized session. Avoid global OffscreenAPI.closeAll() in an addon teardown: it also closes other addons’ windows. Groovy and ZenScript facades close only their own contributions.

Open a child screen or replace the current screens

Push opens a child screen in the same desktop window while keeping its parent available. Back closes that child and reveals the parent. Replacing the root discards all previous screens. Each newly opened screen needs a fresh connecting adapter; do not reuse one that a window has already disposed.

import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.OffscreenAPI;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.integration.vanilla.VanillaUI;
OffscreenAPI.push(window, HelloScreen::new);
boolean returned = OffscreenAPI.pop(window);
window.setUI(new VanillaUI(new HelloScreen()));
int depth = OffscreenAPI.getScreenDepth(window);

import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.*
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.integration.vanilla.VanillaUI
window.pushScreen { HelloScreen() }
val returned = OffscreenAPI.pop(window)
window.replaceScreen(HostUIFactory {
    screen -> VanillaUI(screen as HelloScreen)
}) {
    HelloScreen()
}
val depth = window.screenDepth

import com.sbancuz.offscreen.integration.vanilla.VanillaUI
windows.push(window, { new HelloScreen() })
def returned = windows.back(window)
windows.replace(window, { new HelloScreen() }, { screen -> new VanillaUI(screen) })
def depth = window.getScreenDepth()

import com.sbancuz.offscreen.scaladsl.Offscreen.*
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.OffscreenAPI
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.integration.vanilla.VanillaUI
window.pushScreen(new HelloScreen)
val returned = OffscreenAPI.pop(window)
window.replaceScreen(screen => new VanillaUI(screen.asInstanceOf[HelloScreen]))(new HelloScreen)
val depth = window.getScreenDepth()

val child = Windows.screen("Details", 480, 320);
window.push(child);
val returned = window.back();
window.replace(Windows.screen("New root", 640, 480));
val depth = window.depth;

ZenScript’s Escape action returns to the parent, then closes at the root; a consumed key event can override it. Do not replace a synchronized factory root with a local screen: the server protocol owns that root.
